description: Wallach-framework absorption conflicts, timing rules, and dose-interaction warnings. Sourced from corpus passages where Wallach names specific interactions, plus modern absorption science that aligns with his mechanism statements.

source_legend.wallach-mechanism-extension: Wallach names the mechanism but not the specific interaction; modern absorption science fills in
source_legend.framework-adjacent: Not Wallach-named but supports framework integrity (e.g., common pharmacology)

interactions.trigger: Sustained zinc supplementation above ~30 mg/day depletes copper over time
interactions.rule: If daily zinc > 30 mg: ensure 1-2 mg copper per 15-20 mg zinc; if zinc > 75 mg (clinical): need 4-6 mg copper per Wallach baseline
interactions.wallach_evidence: DDDL Zn entry: 'Zinc accumulates in mammalian kidney, prostate, and eye'; multiple high-Zn protocols (BPH 150 mg/day, testicular atrophy 150 mg/day) require Cu rebalance per his Zn:Cu ratio framing

interactions.trigger: Calcium without magnesium creates arterial calcification risk and muscle cramping
interactions.rule: Wallach maintains Ca:Mg approximately 2:1 (2000 mg Ca + 1000 mg Mg for osteoporosis); never push Ca without Mg
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD osteoporosis protocol: 'calcium and magnesium at 2,000 mg and 1,000 mg per day'; cerebrovascular passage: 'Magnesium deficiency also results in calcification'

interactions.trigger: High phosphorus diet (soft drinks, processed meats, processed cheese) drives calcium loss from bones
interactions.rule: Maintain Ca:P approximately 2:1 in diet AND supplements; avoid phosphate-additive soft drinks and processed foods
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD Paget's Disease + osteoporosis sections: 'correct the dietary calcium/phosphorus ratio'; 'avoid phosphate containing soft drinks'

interactions.trigger: Calcium taken at same meal as iron blocks iron absorption ~50-60%
interactions.rule: Separate iron and calcium by at least 2 hours (modern absorption rule, framework-adjacent)
interactions.wallach_evidence: Wallach does not name this timing rule explicitly; modern absorption science aligns with his general principle that minerals compete for transporters

interactions.trigger: Antacids and PPIs neutralize stomach acid, blocking B12 absorption (intrinsic factor needs acid) and mineral ionization
interactions.rule: Wallach uses betaine HCl as opposite intervention — increase stomach acid; antacid/PPI users face wide-spectrum nutrient malabsorption
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD and DDDL: betaine HCl + pancreatic enzymes 75-200 mg t.i.d. before meals appears in 40+ protocols; mechanism is acid-and-enzyme support, opposite of antacids

interactions.trigger: Low dietary sodium → reduced HCl production → poor B12 absorption (intrinsic factor needs acid) → demyelination + energy crash
interactions.rule: Maintain salt to taste (Himalayan/sea salt); do NOT restrict salt unless specific Wallach-named exception (kidney stones, congestive heart failure with diuretic)
interactions.wallach_evidence: DDDL Na entry + cardiovascular passages: anti-salt-restriction explicit. See evals/2026-06-12-salt.md for full eval

interactions.trigger: Caffeine raises urinary chromium loss for ~12 hours after intake
interactions.rule: If caffeine > 200 mg/day: ensure chromium supplementation at 200+ mcg/day in GTF-aligned form (polynicotinate or nicotinate glycinate)
interactions.wallach_evidence: Rare Earths Cr entry: caffeine + sugar raise urinary Cr loss; 'sugar raises urinary Cr loss 300% for 12 hrs'

interactions.trigger: Sugar intake raises urinary chromium loss 300% for 12 hours
interactions.rule: Reduce processed sugar; supplement Cr in GTF-aligned form if intake unavoidable
interactions.wallach_evidence: Rare Earths Cr entry verbatim quote

interactions.trigger: Uncontrolled industrial-grade fluoride in tap water (sodium fluorosilicate/hexafluorosilicate) at non-titrated dose
interactions.rule: Filter fluoride from drinking water (RO, distillation, activated alumina); fluoride remains essential at LPD baseline (~20 mg/day prescription-grade for osteoporosis), but uncontrolled dosing via water is the problem
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD baseline supplement table shows fluoride at 20 mg/day prescription level for osteoporosis; rhetorical passages flag fluoride water additive as separate dose/source/context. See evals/2026-06-11-fluoride.md

interactions.trigger: Daily-exposure aluminum sources: cookware, antiperspirants, shampoos/conditioners/skincare with aluminum compounds (often hidden in ingredient lists)
interactions.rule: Replace aluminum cookware (stainless / cast iron / glass / ceramic); audit and switch to Al-free deodorant; check personal-care ingredient lists for aluminum compounds (aluminum chlorohydrate, aluminum zirconium, etc.) — these are the high-leverage, easy-to-replace daily exposures
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD Alzheimer's protocol: 'Avoid aluminum cookware, aluminum containing deodorants...' — cookware and personal-care are the recurring concrete examples Wallach names
products_to_check: user lifestyle audit — cookware + deodorant + skincare
interactions.practical_note: Tier-A is high-priority because replacement is cheap and the exposure is daily/chronic. Surface this when relevant.

interactions.trigger: Beverage cans (soft drinks, energy drinks, sparkling waters, fruit juices) — moderate daily exposure
interactions.rule: Prefer glass-bottled when available; for healthy drinks only available in aluminum cans, accept the trade-off at moderate intake (1-3/day). Do NOT make this a recurring talking point in advice — most users cannot eliminate this without losing access to good products or paying significantly more
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD Alzheimer's protocol names 'soft drinks and fruit juices in aluminum cans' alongside cookware, but the practical-replacement burden differs sharply
interactions.practical_note: Tier-B is the practical-trade-off tier. Mention ONCE per answer at most, with the realistic adoption framing. Per brain v2.7 'practical-trade-off inflation' pitfall: don't make this a recurring theme — it's correct Wallach-framework but operationally low-leverage for most users.

interactions.trigger: Fried-food oils (especially repeatedly-heated commercial fryer oils) deliver oxidized lipids and trans fats
interactions.rule: Avoid commercial fryer foods; cook with stable saturated fats (butter, coconut, ghee, lard, tallow); avoid 'oil in name' processed oils (canola, soybean, vegetable oil)
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD cataracts + macular degeneration + many cardiovascular protocols: 'avoid fried foods and margarine'; Adventist longevity data: avoid fried foods extends lifespan ~7 years

interactions.trigger: Chronic alcohol consumption depletes thiamine and damages brain tissue directly (Korsakoff's syndrome)
interactions.rule: Avoid alcohol; if present, supplement B1 100-200 mg/day minimum + full B-complex
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD Korsakoff's syndrome explicitly names alcoholism as cause + B1 deficiency mechanism + 100 mg B1 t.i.d. protocol; Adventist data avoid alcohol extends lifespan

interactions.trigger: Statins block HMG-CoA reductase, simultaneously depleting CoQ10 (cardiovascular cofactor) and blocking the endogenous cholesterol that the cognition WHY-layer eggs/myelin mechanism depends on
interactions.rule: If on statins: surface to user the framework conflict; consider niacin + Cr + fiber + EFA cholesterol-modulation protocol per LPD as Wallach-aligned alternative; supplement CoQ10 100-200 mg/day if user continues statins
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD cholesterol entry: niacin 450 mg b.i.d. time-release + Cr + EFAs + fiber as cholesterol-modulation approach (NOT statins); cerebrovascular protocol uses CoQ10 implicitly via 'baseline supplements'; cognition WHY-layer eggs/cholesterol/myelin mechanism is statin-conflict-relevant
products_to_check: Integris CoQ10+Vit E Succinate (CoQ10 100 mg + Vit E succinate 66 mg)

interactions.trigger: Testosterone elevation (boron, XeraTest, Zn supplementation) requires mineral cofactor floor per Wallach 'explosive mixture' framing
interactions.rule: When supplementing for T (boron + Zn): ensure Cu (4-6 mg), Cr (200+ mcg GTF-aligned), V (50-200 mcg), Li (trace via PDM)
interactions.wallach_evidence: Rare Earths pos 110: 'testosterone surges, high sugar intake and mineral deficiencies are as explosive a mixture as matches, nitroglycerine and gun powder combined' — names Cu, Cr, V, Li specifically
products_to_check: XeraTest stack (need Cu rebalance via Ancestral Liver)

interactions.trigger: High-dose Vit D3 without Mg + K2 cofactors can drive arterial calcification (D3 → ↑Ca absorption → without Mg/K2 → soft-tissue calcification)
interactions.rule: If Vit D3 > 2000 IU/day: ensure Mg 400+ mg/day and K2 (MK-7) 100+ mcg/day; Wallach caps Vit D at 400 IU in cardiovascular context (calcification-conservative)
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD cerebrovascular passage: 'Reduce the amount of vitamin D intake to a maximum of 400 IU/day' (this is a real framework-vs-modern tension)

interactions.trigger: Non-heme iron (ferrous fumarate/gluconate/sulfate in multivitamins) absorbs poorly without ascorbate
interactions.rule: Take iron supplements with Vit C source (orange juice, ascorbic acid 100+ mg)
interactions.wallach_evidence: Not Wallach-direct; modern absorption science aligns with his categorical 'minerals need cofactors' framing

interactions.trigger: Yohimbe is an alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist with stimulant cardiovascular effects
interactions.rule: Avoid yohimbe if user has any blood pressure, anxiety, cardiac, or MAO-inhibitor concern
interactions.wallach_evidence: Not Wallach-named (yohimbe doesn't appear in his books); FDA safety flag

interactions.primary: phosphate additives (soft drinks, processed cheese, baked goods)
interactions.trigger: Industrial phosphate additives upset Ca:P ratio, drive bone calcium loss
interactions.rule: Avoid phosphate-additive soft drinks, processed cheese, baked goods with phosphate emulsifiers
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD Paget's + osteoporosis: 'avoid phosphate containing soft drinks, avoid all phosphate containing supplements'

interactions.secondary: celiac-type intestinal damage, malabsorption, joint pain, mood
interactions.trigger: Undiagnosed food allergens cause celiac-type intestinal changes → malabsorption of essentials → cascade of deficiencies
interactions.rule: Pulse test (Coca pulse test) to identify; common culprits: wheat/gluten, dairy (cow's milk), corn, eggs
interactions.wallach_evidence: LPD references pulse testing in 30+ protocols; celiac-type damage is recurring framing

interactions.trigger: Restricting dietary cholesterol AND blocking endogenous synthesis (statins) starves myelin rebuilding
interactions.rule: Maintain dietary cholesterol intake (eggs daily, red meat 72 oz/month per Wallach); avoid statins; supplement B12 250-400 mcg/day to ensure cholesterol → myelin conversion proceeds
interactions.wallach_evidence: DDDL Alzheimer's protocol food anchor: 'Eat soft-scrambled (not fried) eggs every day and 72 oz. red meat each month to replace cholesterol needed to rebuild myelin'

interactions.trigger: Boron doubles BOTH testosterone AND estradiol per Wallach. In men, elevated estradiol without aromatase awareness can be a concern.
interactions.rule: If boron supplementing for T: monitor estradiol via labs; if E2 trends high, consider DIM (diindolylmethane) or similar (modern aromatase-management, framework-adjacent)
interactions.wallach_evidence: Rare Earths + DDDL boron entries: T AND E double; Wallach doesn't address aromatase management — modern endocrinology gap
